The checks covered the prime-spectrum lifting blocks, the tensor-point naturality proofs (`universalMul_aug` and `mul_eq_tensorPair_universalMul`), the `kwKerAlg` lemmas and the `fourTerm` proof. findings.problem: Both proofs repeat the same argument. They build `hτ` (`Spec.map ψ ≫ kwTensorStruct = t`), prove an ad hoc `hξ` (`schemeHomOverComp (Spec.map ψ) hτ (kwTensorPoint ρ)` equals the target point, shown by `Subtype.ext`, `simp only [schemeHomOverComp_coe, kwTensorPoint, ← Category.assoc, ← Spec.map_comp]`, `congr 2` and `CommRingCat.hom_ext`), and call `G.mul_natural` on `kwTensorPoint includeLeft` and `kwTensorPoint includeRight`. They then rewrite with `hξ` for `includeLeft` and `includeRight` and apply `congrArg Subtype.val`. The two copies differ only in the choice of `ψ` (`εε` or the `kwTensorPair` of two `kwKerAlg`s), the base `t`, and the points `x`, `y`. The `hξ` blocks (lines 424-433 and 536-546) are nearly line-for-line identical apart from how the underlying scheme map is identified. Any change to `kwTensorPoint` or `kwUniversalMul` has to be made twice.
findings.proposed_change:
Add one lemma in the TensorArgument section, for example `kw_rglcktfm_mul_eq_comp_universalMul`, with this statement:
`(T : CommRingCat) (t : Spec T ⟶ Spec (of R)) (ψ : B₁ ⊗[R] B₁ →ₐ[R] T) (hτ : Spec.map (ofHom ψ.toRingHom) ≫ kwTensorStruct B₁ = t) (x y : SchemeHomOver t f) (hx : schemeHomOverComp (Spec.map (ofHom ψ.toRingHom)) hτ (kwTensorPoint B₁ ι hιf includeLeft) = x) (hy : ... includeRight ... = y) : (G.mul t x y).1 = Spec.map (ofHom ψ.toRingHom) ≫ kwUniversalMul G B₁ ι hιf`.
The proof is `have h := G.mul_natural _ t _ hτ (kwTensorPoint .. includeLeft) (kwTensorPoint .. includeRight); rw [hx, hy] at h; exact (congrArg Subtype.val h).symm`.
A companion lemma `schemeHomOverComp_kwTensorPoint` can state: if `Spec.map ψ ≫ ι`-composition identifies `ρ` with a given point `z` (that is, `Spec.map (ofHom (ψ.comp ρ).toRingHom) ≫ ι = z.1`), then `schemeHomOverComp ... (kwTensorPoint ρ) = z`. Then:
- `universalMul_aug` becomes `have := lemma (𝟙 _) εε hτ0 (G.one _) (G.one _) hxL hxR; rw [G.one_mul] at this; exact this.symm`.
- `mul_eq_tensorPair_universalMul` becomes a direct application of the lemma with `ψ := kwTensorPair ..` and the two `lift_comp_include*` facts.
findings.benefit: One statement and one proof of the 'multiplication of two points equals the universal multiplication pulled back along the tensor-pair map' step. The two long theorems shrink to their genuinely different content (the unit case and the kernel case). Changes to `kwTensorPoint` or `kwUniversalMul` then touch a single proof.

findings.problem:
The same two-step prime-lifting argument appears twice, in `kw_rglcktf_specMap_base_surjective` (lines 105-113) and in `kw_rglcktfm_range_truncMul_subset` (lines 449-462).
(1) For a prime `p`, if `I ^ 2 ≤ p` then `I ≤ p`. Both places prove this by hand with `mem_of_pow_mem 2`, `Ideal.pow_mem_pow` and `zero_mem`.
(2) For a surjection `g` and a prime `P` with `ker g ≤ P`, the prime `P.map g` pulls back to `P`. Both places prove this with `map_isPrime_of_surjective`, `PrimeSpectrum.ext`, `comap_map_of_surjective` and `sup_eq_left.mpr`.
The second step is also in Mathlib. The first step is Mathlib's `Ideal.IsPrime.pow_le_iff`.
findings.proposed_change:
Introduce one local lemma, for example `kw_exists_specMap_eq_of_ker_le {R' S' : CommRingCat} (φ : R' ⟶ S') (hsurj : Function.Surjective φ) (P : PrimeSpectrum R') (h : RingHom.ker φ.hom ≤ P.asIdeal) : ∃ q, (Spec.map φ).base q = P`.
Its proof is the current lines 110-113, or alternatively `PrimeSpectrum.range_comap_of_surjective` (range of `comap` equals `zeroLocus (ker f)`).
Then:
- `kw_rglcktf_specMap_base_surjective` becomes `fun p => lemma φ hsurj p (by rw [← Ideal.IsPrime.pow_le_iff (n := 2) two_ne_zero, hker]; exact bot_le)`, with `Ideal.IsPrime.pow_le_iff` applied to the `IsPrime` instance `p.isPrime`.
- In `range_truncMul_subset`, `h𝔐P` follows from the same `pow_le_iff` step, using `Ideal.mk_ker` / `Ideal.Quotient.eq_zero_iff_mem` to show `𝔐 ^ 2 ≤ P.asIdeal`. `q` and `hqP` then come from `obtain ⟨q, hqP⟩ := lemma _ hsurj P h𝔐P`.
findings.benefit: This removes about 15 lines of duplicated ideal-theoretic bookkeeping. The 'square-zero kernel is invisible to primes' fact is stated once, via the library lemma rather than a hand-rolled `mem_of_pow_mem`. The `q` and `hqP` blocks in `range_truncMul_subset` shrink to one line.
